content.title: Graffiti inside the painting｜Realistic interaction gradually draws the hidden world
content.summary: Use first-person real interactions as graffiti triggers: every time a hand, pet, or object completes a visible action, a new line drawing symbol is anchored on the corresponding real-life surface; the symbol is upgraded from a single prompt to an action echo, a hidden object, and a route, and finally the entire set of graphics is connected into a readable world that covers the environment.

quick_start.input_format: Realistic first-person perspective interaction + the first in-painting line draft response + continuous surface path + at least three types of response graphics + real space and fully drawn world in the same frame
quick_start.recommended_input: In the original glass greenhouse, a botanist's glove touches a dew valve, and a brass maintenance beetle approaches; a cyan leaf line drawing appears on the valve's glass shell and stays there; the route is divided into three leaf vein branch lines, one of which is aligned and closed with a small triangular pointing mark Drawer; the botanist only opens it once, and the same cyan veins spread along the metal facade; leaves, soil groove routes, drawer veins and moths are connected to the glass ribs and ground grooves with emerging valves, clouds and waterline symbols; beetles, hands and real structures are all readable
required_anchors: Establish one embodied observer, one responsive subject and the first surface-bound drawing triggered by visible interaction.
Use a second real action to extend the drawing rule onto a different local surface or route.
Reveal one new local figure or motif that visibly inherits an earlier line family.
End on a wider view where prior symbols connect into one coherent environment-wide drawing layer.
usage_steps: Replace the example subject, setting, and surface details with an original concept.
Keep every required anchor and Creative DNA invariant causally visible.
Choose the MiniMax H3 or Seedance 2.0 prompt and fill only the declared variable slots.
Check duration, event order, camera continuity, sound, and anti-copy constraints before generation.
applicable_scope: Use first-person real interactions as graffiti triggers: every time a hand, pet, or object completes a visible action, a new line drawing symbol is anchored on the corresponding real-life surface; the symbol is upgraded from a single prompt to an action echo, a hidden object, and a route, and finally the entire set of graphics is connected into a readable world that covers the environment.
Original 4–15 second concepts that can preserve every required anchor.
MiniMax H3 or Seedance 2.0 projects that need a reusable causal video structure.
not_suitable_for: Requests that copy the source identity, setting, props, dialogue, or shot order.
Concepts that cannot show all required anchors inside the target duration.
Long-form exposition or unrelated multi-location stories without a compact causal chain.

creative_dna.mechanism: Use an embodied observer and one responsive subject to author a diegetic drawing layer through visible real-world actions. Each interaction must add one new surface-anchored symbol that echoes the local object or motion, and later symbols must reuse or connect earlier marks. Escalate from single icon to route, hidden figure and local reflection, then end wide enough to prove the accumulated drawings have become one coherent environment-wide system.

invariants.rule: Establish one embodied observer, one responsive subject and the first surface-bound drawing triggered by visible interaction.
invariants.purpose: Defines who authors the graphic layer and where it belongs.
invariants.ablation_failure: Unmotivated floating stickers make the effect decorative.

invariants.rule: Use a second real action to extend the drawing rule onto a different local surface or route.
invariants.purpose: Proves that the graphic response follows physical behavior.
invariants.ablation_failure: Repeating the same icon over the same hand never builds a world.

invariants.rule: Let accumulated drawings direct attention toward one hidden or newly opened area.
invariants.ablation_failure: Random icons with no search function cannot hand off to discovery.

invariants.rule: Reveal one new local figure or motif that visibly inherits an earlier line family.
invariants.purpose: Creates graphic continuity across separate interactions.
invariants.ablation_failure: A completely unrelated illustration breaks the accumulated system.

invariants.rule: End on a wider view where prior symbols connect into one coherent environment-wide drawing layer.
invariants.purpose: Pays off local marks as a transformed world.
invariants.ablation_failure: Ending on a single sticker or close-up leaves the escalation incomplete.

slots.name: lead_subject
slots.constraint: An original stable subject or pair with a readable role.

slots.name: setting
slots.constraint: A new setting with fixed spatial anchors and no source-specific surface.

slots.name: escalation_variable
slots.constraint: One causal variable that changes through visible stages.

slots.name: performance_rule
slots.constraint: A restrained acting or motion rule that keeps the mechanism legible.

slots.name: camera_grammar
slots.constraint: An information order that proves each state without copying source shot boundaries.

slots.name: payoff
slots.constraint: A clean final physical, informational or social consequence.

slots.name: sound_family
slots.constraint: An original hierarchy of diegetic cues; no unsupported source-audio claim.

anti_copy_exclusions: the source small shaggy dog and first-person human hand
the source domestic hallway, cabinet, rug, ball, bowl and paw prints
the source glowing question mark plus banana, paw, bone, bird and dachshund doodles
the source exact dog search route and final hallway drawing layout

instantiations.concept: In an original glasshouse, a first-person botanist follows a brass maintenance beetle. Touching a dew valve creates one cyan leaf glyph, the beetle rolling a seed capsule draws a route line, opening a propagation drawer reveals an ink moth, and the final wide links leaves, routes, valves and weather symbols across the entire greenhouse skeleton.
